coverage_definition.exact_native: Exactly one full hit, no characters outside that unit, and identical source interval; extra whitespace prevents this status.
coverage_definition.full: The entire raw native-unit character interval lies within rendered atom span.
coverage_definition.gaps: Only whitespace outside native raw intervals; unit-internal whitespace remains unit coverage.
coverage_definition.partial: A nonempty strict subset of the raw native-unit interval intersects.
coverage_definition.partition_check: Each of raw b0 chunks, rule-projected chunks and source leaves separately partitions the whole source and recovers exactly every native-unit character once.

limits: Only fixed protocol/report/artifact, the two specified frozen input copies, and pinned tokenizer files were read. No natural query fields, scores, labels, responses, keys, weights or new corpus were accessed.

All 390 coverage rows were recomputed by raw interval intersections, not by calling source coverage, bridge or probe code. Each partition independently accounts for every native character once and all interunit whitespace.

All 278 payloads and 139 pairs were reconstructed using literal core question/schema/version constants, exact saved export text, canonical JSON serialization and literal cache namespace hashing; no core request constructor was called.
All source provenance receipts match current source hashes/spans/coverage and remain outside the model-visible payload/cache key.
Only current offline request identity was checked. No model execution, historical response cache replay, semantic support, answer quality or label reuse was tested.
Source file hashes are recorded from frozen protocol, not rehashed during this data-only review.

interpretation: Coordinate coverage is not semantic evidence or a rule for reusing support labels/scores.
No natural query, model decision, answer metric, evidence F1 or historical response cache is read or measured.
All 139 source/legacy pairs use an authored offline identity query and offline endpoint/model names; zero transport execution.
Raw b0, rule-projected b0 and leaf granularity are engineering fixtures; no learned Refiner boundaries.
Only standalone requests are built for natural document texts in this probe; conditional and overlap behavior is synthetic-test coverage.
This opt-in source bridge supports standalone/plain_conditional and adds no relation inference, source policy, provider runtime or live default.
Existing core rejects duplicate complete text/source positions; other overlaps on a common atom basis are preserved explicitly, not assumed useful.

next_step.action: Preserve and validate exact source snapshots across actual loader/preprocessing boundary, while separating retrieval representation from JEV decision text.
next_step.observed_code_gap: Current retrieval readers do not preserve new source mode/coordinate/span fields; enrich_chunk_record normalizes chunk.text in place.
next_step.scope: Zero API, no weights/model/gold; same fixed source documents.

request_identity_definition.comparison: For every raw/projected chunk, compare source text to the same-ID/same-order legacy-rendered counterfactual under identical synthetic query, source bridge stateversion and core config. Assert payloads differ only in candidate.text and bindings only in text-derived digest/count.
request_identity_definition.provenance: Local receipt binds current view/hash/spans/coverage to request_key; unchanged full visible decision input may keep key after unselected source text changes, with new provenance receipt.
request_identity_definition.scope: Current offline request identity, never a historical JEV cache hit, semantic decision or paid execution.
request_identity_definition.source_capture: Validate source-mode export text and geometry against immutable index.view; preserve exact bytes, normalized model atoms separately, source order from atom_start.

synthetic_query: Offline text-identity fixture; no model judgment is requested.
